findings.claim: Common prefix/suffix trimming that builds the 'Illegal HTML' message never caps start+end at the shorter string length; when prefix and suffix overlap, substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, an uncaught RuntimeException that aborts the Mojo with a stack trace and skips all remaining keys/files.
findings.evidence:
Trimming logic (L96-111) copied into jshell: value 'x' vs sanitized 'x' throws 'Range [8, 4) out of bounds for length 8' (scratch/diffcrash.jsh); value 'Next ->
' vs 'Next ->' throws 'Range [7, 6)' (scratch/trim.jsh). Sanitizer output was hardcoded, not produced by the real OWASP jar.
findings.reason: Repro of the trimming logic is executed evidence; inputs are exactly the defect class the verifier exists to report. Bound the suffix loop by min(len)-start.

findings.claim: Anchors are matched by position against the English string, so a valid translation that reorders links is flagged; ANCHOR_PATTERN </?a[^>]*> also matches <abbr>, <area>, <audio> giving misleading 'anchor' messages.
findings.evidence: santizeAnchors L150-160. Reasoned.
findings.reason: False positives only (fails closed); no current bundle reorders anchors. ponytail: match anchors as a multiset and tighten pattern to </?a(\s[^>]*)?> when a real translation hits it.

findings.claim: 'Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string' omits key and file, unlike the 'Illegal HTML' message at L111; a build failure cannot be located across ~160 bundles.

findings.claim: Read failures of the file or its derived _en counterpart throw raw RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException used by verify(); the file is also read a second time although contents is already in memory.
